correctness.rationale: The final theorem is restricted to Fibonacci-cube dimensions 6, 7 and 8. The clearing-then-setting bit argument proves distance equals Hamming distance; hence a geodesic flips each coordinate once at most. Exactly F_n first-coordinate edges force >=F_n covering geodesics. I independently regenerated all admissible binary strings/edges and checked every ordered path in actual fibonacci_geodesic_certificate.json against the graph and Hamming endpoint distance: n=6 had 21 vertices/38 edges and 8 valid covering geodesics; n=7 had 34/71 and 13; n=8 had 55/130 and 21. The disjoint extreme coordinate classes yield an edge-general-position set of 2F_n edges; any F_n-geodesic cover yields universal |X|<=2F_n, proving 16,26,42 and cover 8,13,21 exactly. This verifies a finite certificate, not all n.
